beliefs: The outer branch (|x|>=2) is odd with f(x) NEGATIVE for x>0 and POSITIVE for x<0, i.e. f(x) = -sign(x)*|f(|x|)| [E1, E8, E14, E16, E18, E20, E21, E22]
On the positive outer branch |f(x)| follows ln|f| = lnA + p*ln|x| + k*|x| fit to positive data with |x|>=8 [E7, E10, E15, E17, E19, E20]
On the negative outer branch |f(x)| follows a separate ln|f| = lnA' + p'*ln|x| + k'*|x| fit to negative data with |x|>=8 [E8, E14, E16, E18, E20, E21]
Negative-side outer magnitudes exceed positive-side by a factor decaying from ~2.3 at |x|=2.1 to ~1 at |x|>=48, then ~1.03 at large |x| [E10, E14, E16, E18, E20, E21]
f(2)=-60.2 and f(-2)=-67.0; the outer law is continuous through |x|=2 on both sides [E1, E4, E6, E19]
On (0,1) f is exactly 0, with a sharp step to -4.3 at x=1.0 [E5, E9]
On (1,2) f rises smoothly from -4.3 toward ~-30 as x->2- [E3, E4, E5, E9, E19]
On (-2,0) f is a smooth curve: ~+6 near -1, peaking ~+8 near -1.2, then dropping steeply to ~-67 at x->-2- [E3, E6, E24]
There is a genuine jump discontinuity at x=2 on the positive side (from ~-30 at x->2- to -60.2 at x=2) [E19]
There is a jump discontinuity at x=-2: f(-2)=-67.0 exactly, but f(-2.001)=-100.78, so the outer negative branch starts near -100.8 just past -2 and rises in magnitude smoothly [E23, E24]
The negative outer branch is negative (not positive) for x<0, i.e. f(x) = -|f(x)| there; the '-sign(x)' convention only holds for x>0 [E22, E23]
